findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning the RDS MySQL database's underlying storage is not encrypted, exposing data at rest to unauthorized access if the underlying storage is compromised.

publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the RDS instance directly to the internet. Even though the associated security group restricts ingress to the VPC CIDR, enabling public accessibility on a database instance significantly increases attack surface and is a poor secure-default practice for a data store holding credentials and application data.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database password (var.password) and username in plaintext within a PHP config file created via a shell heredoc. EC2 instance user-data is retrievable by anyone with access to the instance metadata service or console/API describe-instance-attribute permissions, exposing the database credentials in cleartext.

The inline policy grants wildcard actions (s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*) on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the EC2 instance. Combined with the instance running in a subnet and holding database credentials, this violates least privilege and would allow full account-wide control over S3, EC2, and RDS resources if the instance is compromised.
